nt: The standard written Hebrew text as we have it today reads “**And I will kindle**.” The ULT follows that reading. In this reading the “I” refers to Yahweh. Other ancient manuscripts read “And he will kindle.” In this reading the “he” refers to Nebuchadnezzar. This is the reading followed by the UST (which reflects Nebuchadnezzar’s soldiers kindling a fire at his command). The UST reflect the “he will kindle” reading because this is the most probable reading in context since the previous verse uses “he” multiple times (referring to Nebuchadnezzar doing the actions) and the rest of this verse uses “he” (referring to Nebuchadnezzar doing the actions). If a translation of the Bible exists in your region, you may wish to use the reading that it uses. If a translation of the Bible does not exist in your region, you may wish to use the reading of the UST.
